items.t: Meituan stock follows senior-note listing toward Hong Kong
sum: Meituan announced on November 3, 2026, that it had applied to list and trade two senior-note tranches on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company's investor-relations page lists the corresponding Hong Kong listing notice and offering circular dated November 4.

The issue comprises CNY 4.5 billion of 2.50 percent senior notes due in 2031 and CNY 3.5 billion of 3.10 percent senior notes due in 2036. According to the Meituan investor-relations page, the notes are being listed for professional investors.

FilingReader, as cited in the latest AD HOC NEWS report, said the financing is intended mainly to refinance existing offshore indebtedness and support general corporate purposes. The senior unsecured obligations are debt rather than equity, so the transaction does not directly increase Meituan's share count. Investors will focus on the resulting interest burden, the liabilities being refinanced and the company's ability to generate cash while competing across its consumer platform businesses.

Meituan stock traded at 9.18 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:30 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The arithmetic change from the 8.05-euro quote in the October 29 report is 14.04 percent. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Meituan stock.

Meituan stock: New senior notes move toward Hong Kong listing
sum: Meituan announced on November 3 that it had applied for the listing and trading of two senior-note tranches on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. A Futubull page carrying the HKEX notice said approval was expected to take effect on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

The proposed listing covers CNY 4.5 billion of 2.50% senior notes due in 2031 and CNY 3.5 billion of 3.10% senior notes due in 2036. The notes are offered exclusively to professional investors under Chapter 37 of the Hong Kong listing rules, and the notice said the offering is not a public sale in the United States.

The structure gives Meituan two debt maturities separated by five years. The 2031 tranche carries the lower coupon, while the 2036 tranche offers a higher coupon for the longer term. The listing application was made under an offering circular dated October 27, according to the notice.

For investors, the transaction adds visibility on the companys access to offshore debt markets but does not by itself change operating earnings. The senior notes are debt obligations rather than equity, so the relevant considerations are future interest costs, refinancing needs and the companys ability to generate cash while competing across its consumer platform businesses.

Meituan stock: CNY 8 billion bond sale targets debt refinancing
sum: Meituan launched CNY 8.00 billion of offshore yuan notes on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, adding a new refinancing instrument as the Chinese food-delivery and local-services provider manages its offshore debt. Reuters reported that the deal comprises CNY 4.50 billion of five-year notes and CNY 3.50 billion of 10-year notes.

The proceeds are aimed mainly at refinancing existing offshore debt and funding general corporate purposes, according to Meituan information cited by Morningstar and Dow Jones. The structure spreads repayment obligations across two maturities rather than concentrating the full amount at one date.

The five-year senior notes carry a 2.50 percent annual coupon and mature in 2031. The 10-year notes carry a 3.10 percent coupon and mature in 2036. Both tranches were priced at par, meaning the proceeds are aligned with the principal amount before fees and other transaction costs.

The notes are expected to receive a Baa1 rating from Moody's and BBB+ ratings from S&P Global Ratings and Fitch, according to the Morningstar and Dow Jones report. Meituan plans to seek a listing for the bonds on the Hong Kong stock exchange, while CLSA, Goldman Sachs and Industrial & Commercial Bank of China are among the joint global coordinators.

For shareholders, the transaction is debt financing rather than an equity issue. It therefore does not directly expand the share count, while the refinancing purpose indicates that the proceeds are intended to manage existing obligations and preserve funds for broader corporate needs. The new coupon burden and the future repayment schedule remain relevant to cash flow and balance-sheet risk.

The deal also gives investors a clearer view of Meituan's funding horizon. The five-year tranche creates a nearer refinancing point, while the 10-year tranche extends part of the liability profile into the next decade. The credit ratings cited for the notes provide a reference for debt investors, but they do not remove exposure to operating performance, competition and refinancing conditions.
The real-time quote of Meituan stock was EUR 8.17 on Lang & Schwarz at 10:01 CET on Friday, October 30, 2026.

Meituan Stock Technicals: Drops 2.81% on Thursday, Testing Support Level
sum: On October 29, 2026: price 69.20 HKD, trend sideways, RSI 38.3, support 69.20, resistance 77.10. technical analysis of meituan stock. Peak — full details here.

Meituan's Hong Kong-listed shares closed at 69.20 HKD on Thursday, October 29, 2026, down 2.81% on the day and sitting just 0.40 HKD above the 3-month low of 68.80, according to exchange data. Over five days the stock has lost 2.95%, and over one month 1.77%. Those monthly figures look mild. The 3-month range tells a harsher story: the high was 96.45.

That gap between a shallow monthly decline and a deep drop from the quarterly peak is the context for today's move. The stock has been sliding for longer than the last 30 days, and it is now testing the floor of its recent range.

Technically, the trend is classed as sideways. The 20-day moving average, which smooths the last 20 trading days of prices into one line, edged down just 0.08% over five days. A flat average suggests the stock has not been in a sharp, accelerating slide recently, but it also shows no sign of recovery.

The price is below the 20-day average of 72.34, which in turn sits under the 50-day average of 75.13. This stacking, with price under the short average and the short average under the long one, is a classic bearish arrangement. It means recent buyers are, on average, holding losses. No new moving-average crossover has formed.

As shown in the chart, the price has settled right on the 20-day support at 69.20, the very level where it closed. Resistance over the same window stands at 77.10. With the price at 0% of that range, the stock sits at the very bottom of its recent trading band.

Momentum gauges paint a mixed picture. The 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI), which measures the speed of recent gains against losses on a 0-100 scale, reads 38.3. That is neutral, though leaning weak; readings below 30 are usually called oversold.

sum: Meituan stock (ISIN KYG596691041) trades at EUR 8.08 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. CEST, while the latest reported quarter showed revenue growth of 14.4 percent to RMB 104.6 billion. The result dated August 28, 2026, returned the company to profitability after a difficult period of food-delivery competition, according to Yahoo Finance.

Meituan reported adjusted net profit of RMB 2.5 billion for the second quarter of 2026, while total segment operating profit reached RMB 3.9 billion. The figures were discussed in the earnings call dated August 28, 2026, and give investors a clearer measure of the recovery than revenue alone.

Chronology shows how that strategy developed. Meituan opened its first Xiaoxiang offline store in December 2025, its second in Ningbo in April 2026, and its third in Hangzhou in July 2026, according to Yahoo Finance. The sequence points to a gradual offline buildout rather than a single large rollout.
The next estimated earnings date is November 26, 2026, according to Yahoo Finance. The date is the next scheduled company event identified in the current market calendar.

sum: Hong Kong’s benchmark finished almost flat on Wednesday, 14 October 2026, after swinging through a 400-point range, as losses in HSBC and lenders outweighed sharp gains in Meituan, Xiaomi and oil producer CNOOC.

The Hang Seng Index closed at 24,314.17 on Wednesday, 14 October 2026, down 31.05 points or 0.13% from Tuesday’s close of 24,345.22. The index opened at 24,282.25 and traded between 24,115.00 and 24,524.63, a range of roughly 410 points, before settling near the middle of its session.

The near-flat finish masked a sharp divergence beneath the surface. Financial and selected technology stocks fell, while consumer internet platforms, hardware maker Xiaomi and energy companies rallied. Asian chipmakers rebounded from heavy losses earlier in the week, but concerns over AI valuations and Chinese semiconductor competition kept investors cautious.

The Hang Seng ended at 24,314.17, a decline of 0.13%. That is about 13.3% below its 52-week high of 28,056.10 and around 8.0% above its 52-week low of 22,518.00. The index has fallen about 5.1% so far in 2026, making Hong Kong one of the weaker major Asian markets this year.

Tuesday’s session had seen a similar pattern, with the index falling as much as 0.8% in the morning before recovering to close 0.3% higher. The US inflation report that dominated global trading on Wednesday was released after the Hong Kong market had closed.

Meituan was the standout gainer, rising 6.64%, while Xiaomi jumped 5.35%, extending its recovery from a steep year-to-date decline. CNOOC added 1.81% as Brent crude rose towards $106.60 a barrel, and China Mobile gained 0.56%. Retail and electronic services shares also advanced.

On the downside, HSBC fell 1.79%, BOC Hong Kong lost 2.58%, Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing declined 1.58% and China Construction Bank fell 1.05%. Tencent slipped 0.42% and AIA eased 0.41%. Among smaller constituents and widely traded names, Akeso dropped 9.6%, Kingboard Laminates lost 5.2% and Z.AI fell 4.8%.

items.t: Chinese Tech Firms Rush to Issue New Shares for AI Investment, Raising Over $41 Billion
sum: Chinese listed technology companies are increasingly turning to equity markets to fund AI investment. Follow-on share offerings in 2026 are expected to exceed $41 billion (approximately ¥6.3 trillion), reaching the highest level since at least 2020. In exchange for securing growth capital, concerns are spreading across the market about dilution of existing shareholders' stakes and deterioration in stock supply-demand dynamics.

The most emblematic case is Alibaba Group (9988.HK). The company announced on August 26 that it had completed the issuance of 710 million new shares. The offering price was HK$112.70 per share, with total proceeds reaching HK$80 billion (approximately ¥1.57 trillion), making it the largest transaction of its kind in the Hong Kong market. The new shares represent approximately 3.57% of the company's outstanding shares after the capital increase.

Regarding the use of proceeds, the company explained that approximately 60% will be allocated to expanding global computing infrastructure, while the remaining approximately 40% will go toward building large-scale AI data centers and upgrading existing cloud infrastructure, including storage, databases, and high-performance networks.

However, the market reaction was harsh. When the offering terms were announced, Alibaba shares fell 8% in early trading on the Hong Kong market on August 24. The offering price was 8.4% below the previous Friday's closing price, which investors viewed negatively. According to Reuters reports, a fund management executive indicated that shareholder dilution would be a negative factor in the short term.

AI startup Z.AI announced plans in July to issue up to 19.78 million shares at HK$1,588 per share. Total proceeds would reach approximately HK$31.41 billion (approximately ¥615 billion), with the offering price representing a 12.99% discount to the previous closing price. The company had already used more than 93% of the net proceeds from its January initial public offering by the end of June, and has indicated it will direct new funds toward research and development, computing resources, and business expansion.
MiniMax also announced in July that it would issue 35.6 million shares at HK$268 per share.

sum: Hong Kong’s stock market started Friday’s session on a strong note, with the Hang Seng Index rising around 2.2% as investors returned to technology stocks. The index gained about 541 points to open near 25,751, marking its strongest level since August 21.

The rally followed gains across global technology markets overnight. Investor sentiment was also supported by expectations that the US Federal Reserve may adopt a less restrictive approach to interest rates if inflation continues to moderate.

Technology shares were among the biggest drivers of Friday’s advance. Comments from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller that indicated a preference for keeping interest rates steady if inflation continues to cool helped ease concerns about further monetary tightening.

A potential Hong Kong listing by Chinese artificial intelligence company Moonshot AI also added to optimism around the region’s technology sector. The company has reportedly filed confidentially for an IPO that could raise about US$3 billion. The broader improvement in risk appetite helped both technology and financial stocks move higher.

Several major technology companies recorded strong gains during the session. Tencent Holdings rose around 2.9% to HK$445.60. The company’s latest share buyback activity also supported sentiment after an HKEX filing showed it repurchased 229,000 shares for approximately HK$100.3 million on September 3.
The gains indicate that the positive mood extended beyond technology stocks, with financial companies also contributing to the market’s advance.

The Hang Seng’s advance came alongside gains in mainland Chinese markets. The Shanghai Composite was trading at around 3,955.85, up 0.35%, while the CSI 300 gained 0.43% to 4,572.28. The Shanghai 50 also edged higher by 0.43% to 2,932.04.

sum: The Hang Seng Index rose about 2.2%, or 541 points, to open at 25,751 on Friday, rebounding from the previous session’s losses and reaching its highest level since August 21, supported by a global tech rally and reduced expectations of a September Fed rate hike.

Global technology stocks gained overnight after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signalled a preference to keep rates steady if inflation continues to cool, easing concerns over tighter monetary policy and boosting risk appetite.
Chinese AI firm Moonshot AI also reportedly confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO that could raise around US$3 billion, further lifting sentiment toward the tech sector.
Tencent Holdings climbed about 2.2% after an HKEX filing showed it bought back 229,000 shares for HK$100.3 million on September 3.
Tech gainers included MiniMax (7.8%), Xiaomi (3.9%), and Meituan (3.7%), while financials rose about 2.4%, led by AIA Group (1.4%), HK Exchanges and Clearing (1.5%), and China Resources Land (2.4%).

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks Rebound 174 Points in Morning Session; Tech Shares Regain Footing as Xiaomi Jumps Over 4%
sum: Hong Kong stocks rebounded on the morning of August 26, following a sharp pullback in the previous session. The Hang Seng Index closed the half-day session at 25,685, up 174 points, or 0.7%. The Hang Seng Tech Index performed even more strongly, rising 72 points, or 1.6%, to 4,660. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index also advanced, gaining 104 points, or 1.2%, to 8,549.

Large-cap technology shares broadly recovered, serving as the primary driver of the market's upward momentum. Xiaomi (01810.HK) surged 4.3% in the morning session to close at HK$28.96, making it the standout heavyweight performer. Meituan (03690.HK) rose 2.2% to HK$78.9; Alibaba (09988.HK) gained 1.5% to HK$115.9; and Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) climbed 1% to HK$446.4.
Chip stocks strengthened in tandem, with SMIC (00981.HK) rising 4.3% to HK$70.8; Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) gaining nearly 7%; and AXera (09992.HK) soaring more than 14%.

Among notable movers, Innovent Biologics (01801.HK) jumped 8.4% in the morning session to HK$108.5, ranking among the top gainers in both the Hang Seng Index and the China Enterprises Index. XPeng-W (09868.HK) rebounded 7.6% to HK$46.6, shaking off the previous day's slump of more than 9%. CMOC Group (03993.HK) rose 7.1%, and Zijin Mining Group (02899.HK) gained 4.9%, lifting the broader non-ferrous metals sector.

Notably, H&H International (01112.HK) skyrocketed 20.6% in the morning session to HK$17.88, hitting an all-time high. Other small- and mid-cap stocks were also active, with Newborn Town (09911.HK) up 14.6%, Jiangxi Copper (00358.HK) up 12.2%, China Nonferrous Mining (01258.HK) up 11%, and ZhongAn Online P&C Insurance (06060.HK) up 10.6%.

Chinese brokerage stocks rallied collectively, buoyed by a dual tailwind of solid earnings and dividend payouts. Market sources indicated that multiple brokerages have recently released interim results showing stable profitability, coupled with clear dividend policies, attracting capital inflows.
The energy sector bucked the trend and declined, with oil and coal stocks underperforming and serving as the primary drag on the broader market's gains.

sum: Hong Kong stocks suffered a significant pullback after five consecutive sessions of gains, with the Hang Seng Tech Index plunging 3.61% in a single day. Alibaba (09988.HK), conducting its first share placement since listing, saw its stock crash more than 8%, becoming the heaviest weight dragging down the broader market.

As of the August 24 close, the Hang Seng Index fell 1.89% to around 25,465 points, with full-day main board turnover remaining elevated. The Hang Seng Tech Index fell even harder, closing at approximately 4,582 points, down 3.61%, with nearly all constituents finishing in negative territory.

Alibaba's share placement raised as much as HK$80 billion (approximately $10.2 billion). Upon the announcement, the stock quickly broke through the placement price, falling more than 10% intraday before closing down over 8% at around HK$111 (approximately $14), making it the worst performer among both Hang Seng Index and Hang Seng Tech Index constituents. This marks Alibaba's first share placement since its listing, and market concerns over equity dilution were directly reflected in the share price.

Other major Chinese internet stocks also came under pressure. Xiaomi (01810.HK) fell over 4%, Baidu (09888.HK) and Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) both dropped more than 3%, and Meituan (03690.HK) declined over 2%.

Semiconductor, optical communications, and AI application concept stocks bore the brunt of the selling. China's Zhongji Innolight (300308.SZ) tumbled over 11%, AI large-model company MiniMax fell over 10%, Zhipu dropped over 10%, SMIC (00981.HK) slid nearly 8%, Chinese chip designer Montage Technology (688008.SS) fell over 8%, and Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) declined over 5%. The chip and AI large-model sectors faced heavy selling pressure overall, reflecting investors' profit-taking sentiment on high-valuation tech stocks.

In stark contrast to the dismal performance of tech stocks, the new consumer sector bucked the trend. Mixue Group (02097.HK) surged over 7%, Pop Mart (09992.HK) rose over 4%, and Mao Geping (01318.HK) gained nearly 3%, indicating that capital is rotating toward more defensive consumer-oriented names amid sector rotation.

items.t: Kimi K3 Wipes $3.3T From Chip Stocks: Moonshot Moves Toward Hong Kong IPO
sum: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, released July 16 at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, erased more than $3.3 trillion in global semiconductor market value in a matter of days — and on Sunday, the Beijing-based startup responded to its own market-moving moment by circulating a shareholder resolution seeking approval for a Hong Kong initial public offering within six months.

The selloff drove the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index more than 20% below its late-June peak, crossing the technical threshold for a bear market. It marked the worst weekly rout for chipmakers since April 2025. Before any enterprise buyer routes sensitive code or business logic through the Kimi API, one number deserves to sit next to the cost comparison: independent testing found K3's hallucination rate climbed to approximately 51% even as its raw accuracy improved — meaning roughly one in two factual assertions from the model may be wrong. The full model weights needed for independent verification are not scheduled for public release until July 27.

Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model — the largest open-weight AI system ever released — with a 1-million-token context window and native vision support. The 2.8-trillion figure is the total parameter count across all 896 specialized expert subnetworks, but only 16 of those experts activate for any given token, meaning the model's per-token compute cost is closer to 30–50 billion active parameters in practice. That sparse-routing architecture is what makes a model of this size economically viable to serve.
Three architectural innovations distinguish K3 from its predecessor, Kimi K2.6:

Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) replaces standard quadratic self-attention in most layers with a more efficient hybrid linear attention, interleaving full attention with linear attention in a 3:1 ratio. In Moonshot's smaller research model, KDA cut key-value cache usage by up to 75% and decoded up to six times faster than a comparison system at 1-million-token context. K3-specific numbers await the July 27 technical report.
Attention Residuals (AttnRes) let each transformer layer selectively retrieve representations from arbitrary earlier layers rather than accumulating them uniformly.

Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 Sparks $30B Valuation Race
sum: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model sparked global tech and crypto selloff, pushing the Chinese startup's valuation past $20 billion

A year ago, most investors outside China hadn't heard of Moonshot AI. This week, the Beijing startup wiped billions off chipmakers' market caps and dragged bitcoin below $63,000 with a single model release.
Moonshot released Kimi K3 on July 16, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model built on a sparse mixture-of-experts design that activates just 16 of its 896 experts per task.

On a closely watched coding leaderboard, it topped offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI, though it still trails the newest flagship models from both companies on broader benchmarks. Full open weights are due July 27.
Traders dubbed it a "Kimi moment", echoing DeepSeek's 2025 debut, which erased roughly $600 billion from Nvidia's market value in a single session.

Chip and AI stocks slid across Asia and Wall Street, while bitcoin, ether and other major cryptocurrencies fell as investors treated the release as a fresh challenge to assumptions about US compute dominance.

Moonshot's valuation has increased from $4.3 billion at the end of 2025 to a value exceeding $20 billion, and reports have emerged suggesting further negotiations which would see their value pushed up to $30 billion.

items.t: Memory Chip Stocks Hit by Black Storm: SanDisk Plunges 12% Overnight, SK Hynix Falls Another 7% in Premarket
sum: The global memory chip sector is experiencing a violent wave of selling. After suffering heavy losses during the late-night US trading session on July 15, related stocks extended their collapse in premarket trading on July 16, reflecting extreme investor anxiety over the segment's near-term outlook. Meanwhile, Chinese ADRs surged against the tide, emerging as one of the few bright spots in the market.
Panic Spreads: From Overnight Crash to Extended Premarket Losses

The sell-off reached its first climax during the July 15 session. According to real-time trading data disclosed by NetEase News, as of 11:00 p.m. that evening, even as the three major US indices posted modest gains—the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.38%, the Nasdaq Composite added 0.19%, and the S&P 500 edged up 0.19%—the memory chip sector suffered a stampede-like decline. SanDisk shares plummeted more than 12%, leading the sector's losses; South Korean memory giant SK Hynix crashed over 10%; Western Digital, Seagate Technology, and Micron Technology all fell more than 7%.

Panic quickly spread across the broader semiconductor sector. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) staged a dramatic intraday reversal, swinging from gains to losses and ultimately closing down nearly 3%. Multiple chip stocks that had been trading higher earlier in the session turned negative as a result. AMD and Marvell Technology dropped over 5%, Intel fell close to 5%, and ARM, Texas Instruments, and ON Semiconductor broadly declined between 1% and 2%.

After just one trading day, the fleeing capital has not returned. Ahead of the US market open on July 16, all three major index futures pointed lower, with Dow futures dipping 0.02%, Nasdaq 100 futures widening their losses to 0.47%, and S&P 500 futures falling 0.17%. The decline in memory chip stocks not only failed to stabilize but worsened. Premarket data showed SK Hynix falling another nearly 7%, SanDisk and Western Digital down over 5%, Seagate Technology and AMD off more than 3%, and Micron Technology, Intel, and Marvell Technology all down over 2%. Among tech giants, Nvidia was weak in premarket trading, falling over 1%, while Google and Microsoft posted gains.

NIO Stock Extends Rally: China’s 'Hottest' Memory-Chip Company Just Won An EV Backer
sum: - Nio invested $23.3 million in CXMT’s IPO amid pressure from memory-chip costs on EV makers.
- Nio unit, Nio Power, received 18.24 million CXMT shares with an 18-month lock-up.
- CEO William Li has previously said that memory costs have added nearly 20,000 yuan to each ES8.

U.S.-listed shares of Nio, Inc. (NIO) extended their rally for a second day after the EV maker invested 158 million yuan ($23.3 million) in the IPO of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's largest DRAM maker, as soaring memory-chip prices continue to pressure automakers.
Nio’s U.S.-listed stock jumped 2% on Tuesday, but shares are down 0.4% overnight heading into Wednesday.

Nio's unit, Nio Power Technology (Hefei), was allotted 18.24 million shares, or about 0.27% of CXMT's offering, with an 18-month lock-up period. CXMT is China's largest DRAM producer and the world's fourth-largest by market share, CnEVPost noted.

The IPO is priced at 8.66 yuan per share and could raise as much as 66.6 billion yuan if the over-allotment option is exercised, making it China's second-largest IPO ever. The offering values the company at about 579.2 billion yuan. Nio joins Xiaomi, Alibaba Cloud, Tencent, Meituan, Chery and ZTE as strategic investors in the offering.

sum: Alibaba shares spike 12% in Hong Kong as T-Head chips, AI revenue fuel earnings optimism
UBS and Jefferies project the firm’s revenue to accelerate to 9% in June quarter, well above the 3% recorded in the previous quarter

Shares of Alibaba Group Holding surged to a high of 13.8 per cent in Hong Kong on Wednesday as equity analysts expect revenue to reaccelerate in the June quarter, driven by growing demand for artificial intelligence and narrowing losses in food delivery.

The gain, the strongest this year, came before the company closed up 12.2 per cent at HK$107.5 (US$13.71). Rivals Tencent Holdings and Meituan saw their shares grow 3.8 and 3.3 per cent, respectively, while the Hang Seng Tech Index increased by nearly 5 per cent.

Total revenue for the June quarter was expected to rise by 9 per cent, according to reports by both Jefferies and UBS on Wednesday. That would mark a sharp improvement from the 3 per cent revenue growth recorded in the previous quarter.

Of this, the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect recorded net purchases of HK$12.55 billion (approximately $1.6 billion), while the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect saw net purchases of HK$7.97 billion (approximately $1.0 billion), indicating that mainland Chinese investor confidence in the Hong Kong market is gradually recovering.

Tencent-related concept stocks generally moved higher. Maoyan Entertainment (01896.HK) jumped over 8%, while Tongcheng Travel (00780.HK) and ZhongAn Online P&C Insurance (06060.HK) followed suit. items.t: Will share buy-backs help Chinese big tech companies rescue battered valuations?
sum: Firms like Tencent and Alibaba are trying to boost investor confidence in the sector, whose stock prices have recently hit alarming lows

Chinese tech giants including Tencent Holdings, Alibaba Group Holding, Meituan, and Xiaomi have launched aggressive share buy-back programmes to revive investor confidence amid continuing scepticism towards the sector, while analysts suggest that a bottoming out could soon be in sight.

Plagued by stock prices that have hit alarming lows in recent trading cycles, the tech heavyweights are leaning on massive share repurchase programmes and high-profile appearances by company leaders to boost market confidence.
“With solid net cash positions and outstanding buy-back programmes, we expect companies to accelerate the buy-back pace,” Citi Research analysts said in a recent note.

Wang Xing Calmly "Responds to Everything" at Meituan's General Meeting: From Food Delivery Wars to Shrinking Market Value and Past Five - Year "Two Major Mistakes"
sum: On June 26, Meituan's annual general meeting of shareholders was held. Previously, due to the subsidy war worth tens of billions in the food delivery and instant retail sectors, Meituan's performance turned from profit to loss in 2025, and its stock price dropped significantly. This meeting has attracted significant market attention.

At the meeting, Wang Xing responded to the slump of the stock price and stated that he had no plan to reduce his holdings. He reviewed two strategic mistakes in the past five - year strategies, namely the late start of overseas expansion and the operation of Meituan Select. He proposed that future business investments would strictly adhere to financial discipline. CFO Chen Shaohui said that the company's value was seriously underestimated and planned to restart the stock repurchase. He also disclosed that Meituan's overseas investment scale exceeded 65 billion yuan, covering various cutting - edge technology sectors. After the lock - up period expires, Meituan will cash out the listed targets at an appropriate time.

In response to concerns about the competition for platform entry in the AI era, Wang Xing believes that AI will not bring a disruptive impact in the short term, but Meituan will continue to make arrangements and follow the technological development through investment and cooperation.

At the industry level, the high - cost subsidy competition has dragged down the entire industry. However, Meituan's share of high - unit - price food delivery orders is stable, and the operation of its food delivery business has been continuously reducing losses. Coupled with the introduction of new regulatory rules on food delivery subsidies, institutions' judgments on its prospects are divided.

Overall, after the huge subsidy war, Meituan's strategy has completely shifted to a repair mode of reducing losses, repurchasing stocks, and disposing of investments. However, whether the subsidy competition has ended and whether the profit inflection point can be sustained still need to be verified by subsequent operating data.
After the subsidy war worth tens of billions and the market value falling below HK$400 billion, Meituan has reached a new strategic juncture.
